einzeiler: Angela Duckworth on bringing out your best and the limits of grit
kurzfassung: Psychologist Angela Duckworth discusses how our surroundings shape our behavior and success. She explores why achieving goals rarely brings happiness and why grit is not always enough. The conversation also covers personal reflections, environmental changes, and the impact of the people around us.
stichpunkte: How environments shape behavior before we realize it
Why achieving goals rarely delivers happiness
The limits of grit and why it is not always enough
Personal reflections on past experiences and apologies
The impact of surroundings on performance and agency
beschreibung:
Angela Duckworth (Situated: Find the People and Places That Bring Out Your Best, Grit) is a psychologist, MacArthur Fellow, and professor at the University of Pennsylvania. Angela returns to the Armchair Expert to discuss nearly drowning while trying to save her mother, apologizing 15 years later to an author she treated poorly, and how a graduate student’s critique of Grit changed the direction of her work. Angela and Dax talk about why achieving goals rarely delivers happiness, how Leon Marchand changed his environment to break Michael Phelps’s world record, and why the people around us deserve more credit for our success. Angela explains why grit isn’t always enough, how our surroundings shape our behavior before we realize it, and why changing your situation can actually give you more agency.
